http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/28/nepal.text: At least 1,924 people are missing and at least 579 have been killed after devastating floods tore through the border region between Nepal and Tibet, as rescuers reached some of the worst-hit areas for the first time.The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said on Friday that early estimates suggested about 93,000 people may have been affected by Wednesday's disaster and warned that the death toll was expected to rise."The trauma of this event is enormous," said David Fisher, the IFRC's head of delegation for Nepal.He said washed-out roads and bridges, along with disrupted mobile phone coverage and electricity supplies, meant rescuers had still been unable to reach some of the hardest-hit areas.Nepalese police put the country's death toll at at least 547 on Friday, while Chinese state media has confirmed five deaths on the Tibetan side of the border.Professional rescue teams have now reached the main disaster zone in Tibet. China's Xinhua news agency said teams from Tibet and neighbouring Sichuan arrived at the "core rescue site" on Friday afternoon.Chinese state media also said 499 residents and 555 tourists had been evacuated from the disaster zone. The nationalities of the tourists were not immediately disclosed.More than 100 trapped near hydropower tunnelIn Nepal, the military said it had located people trapped around the Trishuli 3A hydropower project and was working to bring them to safety.More than 100 people remained trapped in the area, while around 350 workers and residents had already been rescued, army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet said.Two helicopters had been dispatched, but rescue efforts were being complicated by the difficulty of locating the tunnel entrances following the devastation.The operation comes two days after a glacial collapse triggered a vast flow of ice, rock and debris through river valleys near Nepal's border with China's Tibet region.The US Geological Survey said the debris flow and flooding travelled nearly 100 kilometres along the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi rivers, destroying buildings and infrastructure and cutting a vital highway linking Nepal and China.Fears of further floodingNepalese authorities urged people to move to higher ground on Friday following reports that a dam in Tibet had burst, raising fears of further flooding downstream.China temporarily halted rescue operations after a lake formed by huge quantities of debris began overflowing. State media later said the danger posed by the lake was decreasing and rescue operations were proceeding "in an orderly manner".It was not immediately clear whether the overflowing lake was connected to the reported dam burst.The effects of the disaster have also been felt downstream in India, where authorities said seven bodies believed to be flood victims had been recovered from rivers flowing from Nepal.Nepal has appealed for international financial assistance but said its own emergency services were currently able to handle rescue operations without foreign teams.Foreign ministry spokesman Lok Bahadur Chhetri said Nepal would request specialised assistance or expertise if required. Chinese President Xi Jinping has offered Beijing's help.

https://www.lowkickmma.com/alana-cook-ey.text: Alana Cook will be making history in a few ways with her Oktagon MMA foray over the weekend. At Oktagon 93 on September 12th, Cook clashes with Niamh Kinehan, with the former becoming the first Canadian woman to compete for the powerhouse European MMA promotion. Even beyond that historical trend, ‘The Alanamal’ will also become the first indigenous woman as well as the first member of Niagara Top Team to fight for OKMMA. While Alana Cook has previously spoken in French, she has also gone the extra step to learn Czech for her fight in Brno. Cook emphasized the importance of wanting to immerse herself in the culture of the Czech Republic as she spoke on MMA Canada ahead of the bout. Alana Cook has been refining her skills at Niagara Top Team with names like Jasmine Jasudavicius, Aaron Jeffery, and Mike Malott frequently grinding it out in the gym. Another NTT compatriot, Cam Nelson, also had a fruitful and historic promotional debut in his own right at UFC Shanghai recently. The electric nature of the room, especially on Monday per the BC native, carries a particular energy that seems destined to course through the mixed martial arts world in a generational fashion. Alana Cook respects Niamh Kinehan’s polished game but outlines path to victory at Oktagon 93 Alana Cook prepares to battle ‘The British Razor’ here, and she has quite the Muay Thai pedigree. Addressing the litany of titles in the WBC, WMO, and more that her adversary on Saturday has captured, Cook said [via MMA Canada ], “All the letters, all the alphabet letters she’s got [laughs].” When assessing her opponent Kinehan’s stand-up pedigree and spotless record within MMA so far, Alana Cook stated [via MMA Canada ], “Well, I’ve taken a few O’s before from people, so it’s business as usual. Her name’s Niamh Kinehan, so I believe she’s Irish or British. I’m not quite sure, but props to her. Like, any woman that can do that, that’s very incredible. She’s very talented. I’ve obviously watched her fights and she’s got a really, really big following. So, the way I’m looking at it is, the audience already knows what she can do, but no one knows what I can do yet. So, I’m really excited to show Oktagon what I can do.” “Obviously she’s very talented. She’s very dangerous. I haven’t looked at the stats. I really don’t like looking at that. I always just kind of pretend or think of myself as the underdog. I just consider myself always the underdog going into it and being like, you know what, I’m gonna have to be scrappy. I’m gonna have to. This is going to be the toughest fight of my life. I think just always having that mentality of, she could whip out anything, right?” “Just being prepared for everything. Again, luckily at NTT [Niagara Top Team] there’s so many different looks and so many different people that come in, that I get to see all those different styles. So yeah, I have a lot of respect for her. I think she has a very, very polished style. But I’m an ugly fighter, baby. So, let’s go. I think it’s going to be a lot of fun and I think we’re both going to build up the fight. It’s going to be good. https://zizonline.com/prince-drew-to-hos.text: National Prince-Drew to Host Caribbean Tech Conference in November Published October 7, 2026 · 2 min read f X w ✉ Listen to this article · 2 min ■ BASSETERRE — Diani Jimesha Prince-Drew, wife of the Prime Minister, will host a Caribbean Conference under the Fostering the Future Together initiative in St. Kitts and Nevis this November, she announced following a First Spouses’ luncheon hosted by United States First Lady Melania Trump in New York. Prince-Drew attended the Fostering the Future Together Coalition Luncheon on the margins of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, joining fellow First Spouses and other distinguished leaders. During the gathering, Trump announced a series of regional Fostering the Future Together engagements, including the Caribbean conference to be hosted by Prince-Drew, a European Regional Meeting in Poland, and an ASEAN engagement in the Philippines. “The luncheon provided a valuable opportunity to deepen our shared commitment to expanding opportunities for children through technology and education,” Prince-Drew said in a social media post. She said she also met with Trump, First Lady of Poland Marta Nawrocka, and First Lady of the Philippines Liza Araneta Marcos to further discuss the upcoming regional engagements. The Caribbean conference will be held under the theme “Empowering Caribbean Children for the Digital Age,” with a focus on four key pillars: AI in education, EdTech tools, online protection and digital skills. “We look forward to welcoming First Spouses, senior officials, technology leaders and other partners to Saint Kitts and Nevis this November,” Prince-Drew said, describing the gathering as an opportunity to bring together regional and international perspectives and advance practical action supporting Caribbean children in a digital world. https://www.politico.eu/article/portugal.text: Portugal's foreign ministry on Tuesday slammed Mark Rutte after the NATO chief said that for Lisbon, Russia was a distant and less relevant threat. "Portugal, its Government and its people have never been in any doubt about which side of history they stand on," the ministry said on X. "It is regrettable that the NATO Secretary General should speak so lightly on such a serious matter. "Mark Rutte should know better than to overlook the countries and governments that stand firmly by Ukraine and fully understand the threat posed by Russia," it added. Advertisement Advertisement Rutte told Dutch TV last week that Southern European countries like Spain and Portugal see Russian aggression as remote. "Sometimes I tell our allies in Spain or Portugal, who say, 'It's far away, and what happens in Russia mainly affects Poland'" that "Russia's latest missiles take 5 minutes longer to reach Lisbon than Warsaw," he said. NATO spokesperson Allison Hart said: "It is clear that all Allies agree that Russia is a threat ... and while all governments understand the threat, the Secretary General often highlights for public audiences who may not be as engaged on security issues how very close this threat is to all Allies." Since Russia's full-scale attack on Ukraine in 2022, Spain has given €1.5 billion in military and humanitarian aid to Ukraine, or 0.2% of its GDP, according to the Kiel Institute's Ukraine Support Tracker. Portugal has donated €390 million, or 0.18% of GDP — far below Germany and frontline countries. However, a Eurobarometer poll taken this spring found that 92% of those surveyed in Portugal saw Russia's invasion of Ukraine as a security threat to the EU, while 82% of those Spain thought the same. The average for the EU was 76%.
